The Budget Set

Draw the region of bundles you can afford, set by prices and your money. If the two goods together cost more than your money, that bundle is out. The borderline is the budget line. When one good gets pricier, the line rotates inward. With more money, the line shifts outward in parallel. The budget set and slope formulas are below. For example, a 6,000-won allowance buys 🍎 apples at 1,000 won each and 🍌 bananas at 2,000 won each. Apples alone, you can get six; bananas alone, three. If apples rise to 2,000 won, only three apples fit the budget.

Bp,w={x∈R+2:p1x1+p2x2≤w}B_{p,w} = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^2_+ : p_1 x_1 + p_2 x_2 \le w\}Bp,w​={x∈R+2​:p1​x1​+p2​x2​≤w}
slope=−p1p2\text{slope} = -\frac{p_1}{p_2}slope=−p2​p1​​

  3. The probe bundle costs p⋅b=1⋅30+2⋅15=60=wp \cdot b = 1 \cdot 30 + 2 \cdot 15 = 60 = wp⋅b=1⋅30+2⋅15=60=w. The budget is fully spent, so Walras' law holds and the point bbb lies on the budget line.
